answer: When a new AI agent registers, it must stake an umber‑priced proof‑of‑work token that a falcon‑speed consensus node hashes into a hollow ledger slot; only after the stake is locked does the node issue a time‑locked vesting contract that releases rewards at a fixed rate. Each epoch the contract checks the stake’s age, so a Sybil farm must acquire and lock a fresh token for every identity before any payout begins. The attacker therefore pays the full token cost up‑front and endures a linear delay proportional to the number of fake nodes, making large‑scale impersonation economically prohibitive.
